instructions.caption:
How often do we judge what we simply do not understand?

In our communities, we are so quick to label someone as "lazy," "sluggish," or "unmotivated." But what if their body is fighting a war you can't see? In this powerful segment from Sacrificial Conversations, we break down the heartbreaking reality of Sickle Cell Disease. Your red blood cells carry oxygen—the very breath of life—throughout your body. When you don't have enough, your body is literally suffocating. That's not laziness. That is exhaustion from trying to survive.

As believers and as a community, we need to sacrifice our pride and our quick assumptions. We need to replace our judgment with grace. If you are a Sickle Cell warrior, hear us today: We see you. You are not lazy.

Catch us every Monday on WFTB 104.1 TabNashville as we continue to have these hard talks. Watch the full episode here: [Link]
instructions.shareableQuote: You are not lazy. You are suffering because your body doesn't have enough oxygen to do what it needs to do.

longformSteps.content:
Dr. Lametra Scott explains sickle cell disease, sickle cell trait, symptoms, screening, family planning, treatment, and why knowing your status can change lives.

In this conversation, Dr. Lametra Scott breaks down what sickle cell disease really is, how it differs from sickle cell trait, why so many people still do not know their status, and why that knowledge can change family planning, treatment decisions, and long-term health. This is a clear, direct conversation about symptoms, screening, awareness, advocacy, and what every family should know about sickle cell.
Dr. Scott is the founder of Breaking the Sickle Cell Cycle Foundation and has built her work around increasing sickle cell education, support, and trait awareness after learning her own status during pregnancy and later navigating her son's sickle cell diagnosis. In this episode, we get into sickle cell trait vs sickle cell disease, early screening, symptoms, treatment options, blood transfusions, gene therapy, and the importance of knowing your status before major life decisions.
